subject: Retrieval validation sprint — readout and RAG tuning recommendations
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@novapulse.com>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@novapulse.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Retrieval validation sprint — readout and RAG tuning recommendations

Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo today — really appreciate the walkthrough of NovaPulse's use cases (patient intake summarization + clinician Q&A). As promised, here is a concise readout from our quick validation sprint plus recommended next steps to put a small canary into production without disrupting your SLA targets.

Summary of findings (engineer-friendly):
- Document coverage: our sampling of 500 docs (mix of policies, intake notes, and discharge summaries) showed a median top-k recall of 0.78 when using your current vectordb config (512-d, cosine) with a 400-token chunk size.
- Retriever sensitivity: recall drops ~9% when k < 5 for longer context questions; for short factual questions (single-entity lookups) k=3 was sufficient.
- Reranker impact: adding a lightweight cross-encoder reranker improves precision@1 by ~7pp versus pure dense retrieval for safety-critical queries, with a 25-40ms token penalty per call on our L4 machines.
- Model fit: for candidate generation we recommend using an instruction-tuned 7B variant (Redwood-7b-inst) for cost-conscious UAT, and Redwood-13b-quant for tighter truthfulness and longer generation budgets.

Key concerns we flagged:
- Quality regression risk: changes to tokenizer normalization in your ingestion pipeline caused subtle tokenization drift in ~6% of documents; this produced hallucinations in a small subset of generative prompts.
- Latency budget: with the cross-encoder reranker enabled, end-to-end P95 for your interactive Q&A flows reaches ~520ms on our dedicated pools (target was 350ms). We propose an asynchronous fallback path for sessions that need sub-350ms latencies (fast path: dense-only; slow path: dense+rerank).

Deliverables attached:
- novapulse-eval-kit-v1.zip (prompt sets, sample docs, canonical questions, evaluation harness)
- retriever-reranker-benchmarks-20270829.csv (raw metrics from the sprint)

Recommended next steps (short, actionable):
1) Approve a 2-week canary to run on a 10% traffic slice using Redwood-7b-inst + reranker in strong-consistency mode.
2) Devs: sync on tokenization normalization fix (we've included a suggested preprocessor in the eval kit).
3) Schedule a run of the full 5k-document bench we included in the Drive link; Ben will share a cost estimate for the run.

Are you available tomorrow for a 30-minute call to lock down the canary window? If not, tell me times that work and we will slot it.

Thanks,
Irene

Subject: Re: Retrieval validation sprint — readout and RAG tuning recommendations

Thanks Irene — this is helpful and much appreciated. A few quick clarifications from our side before we sign off on the canary:

1) For the reranker you mention a 25-40ms token penalty — can you clarify if that is per-candidate or per-request? Our SLA is sensitive to per-request overhead.
2) On model selection: Redwood-7b-inst sounds like a reasonable first step. Can you share a small sample of generation differences between 7b-inst and 13b-quant for our prompts so our PMs can see the delta?
3) Regarding the tokenization drift: is the suggested preprocessor a breaking change for our historical data ingestion? We need to know if we must reindex prior docs.

We're broadly OK with a 10% canary but want to avoid full reindexing unless necessary. If the preprocessor can be run at query time as a patch, that would be ideal.

Happy to hop on a call tomorrow at 10:00am PT — Priya and I can make that.

Best,
Alex

Alex Kim
VP Product, NovaPulse
alex.kim@novapulse.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retrieval validation sprint — readout and RAG tuning recommendations

Alex / team — quick technical replies to Alex's questions: 

1) Reranker timing: the 25-40ms is per-request for the top-5 candidate set when we run a lightweight cross-encoder (we batch 5 candidates in a single forward and amortize some overhead). If you reduce the candidate set to k=3 the penalty falls to ~18-22ms. We can also use a distilled re-ranker (Redwood-rerank-small) that trades ~3-4pp precision for ~12ms latency savings.

2) Sample diffs between Redwood-7b-inst and Redwood-13b-quant: I uploaded a short CSV to the benchmark S3 link showing 20 prompt/responses from your evaluation kit. High-level: 13b-quant reduces unsupported-token hallucinations on long-context synthesis and improves factuality on 6/20 probes we ran (F1 uplift ~0.06). 7b-inst is cost-efficient and comparable on short completion tasks.

3) Tokenization patch: the preprocessor we suggested is non-destructive — it normalizes boundary whitespace and certain unicode punctuation at query-time. It does not require a full reindex; however, for the highest retrieval recall on historic long docs we recommend a one-off re-embedding job (optional) if you want deterministic parity. We can provide a staged reindex script that runs at low priority.

Operational suggestion: start with the canary using k=5 + distilled reranker (Redwood-rerank-small) and monitor precision@1, latency P95 tiering, and hallucination rate on the canonical prompt set. If precision@1 is < 0.72 after 48 hours, escalate to full cross-encoder.

I've included cost estimates in the Drive doc and a quick Bash snippet for running a re-embed (non-blocking).

- Ben

Perfect — thanks Ben and Alex. Confirming next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

- Canopy: 10% traffic canary starting Wed 09/01 00:00 UTC, running 14 days.
- Config: k=5, Redwood-7b-inst generator, Redwood-rerank-small (distilled) for initial canary. Fallback rules: dense-only fast-path if per-request latency > 350ms for a session.
- Deliverables before start: 1) final eval kit + canonical prompt set (we uploaded v1; Ben to push v2 with the sample 13b comparisons), 2) preprocessor script (query-time patch) — Dev to share staging link, 3) cost estimate and re-embed playbook (Ben).
- Monitoring: we will track precision@1, recall@5, hallucination_rate (as a percent of QA probes flagged), and P95 latency. We'll create alerts if precision@1 drops > 5pp week-over-week or if hallucination_rate exceeds 3%.

Alex / Priya — I'll send a calendar invite for 10:00am PT tomorrow to finalize the canary window; please accept if that time still works. After that call we'll move the canary to a runbook and give you a one-click toggle in the Console.

Thanks all — excited to get this running.

Irene
